title: Largest Run Sum on a Loop
statement:
The integers in nums are arranged in a loop: after the last element comes the first one again. A run is a non-empty stretch of consecutive elements along the loop, so it may wrap from the end back to the start. A run can use each position at most once, so it never covers more than the whole loop.

Return the largest sum of any run.

examples.why: The run 2, 3, 4 wraps from the end to the start. Without wrapping, the best is 2 + 3 = 5.
Every number is negative, so the best run is the single -1. The run cannot be empty.
The wrapped run 5, 5 skips the -2. Going around twice to collect more fives is not allowed.

hints: Ignore the loop for a moment: the best non-wrapping run is the classic running-sum problem. What does a wrapping run look like?
A wrapping run takes a prefix and a suffix of the array. What is left out is one contiguous middle stretch.
Maximising prefix + suffix is the same as minimising the middle stretch you leave out: total − (smallest run sum). Watch the case where that would leave out everything.

explain.intuition:
Any run either stays inside the array or wraps around the end. The best non-wrapping run comes from Kadane's scan: keep the best sum of a run ending here, and restart when carrying the past only hurts.

A wrapping run is everything except one contiguous stretch in the middle. So its best sum is total − (smallest run sum), and the same scan with min instead of max finds that smallest run. One catch: if every number is negative, the smallest run is the whole array, and "everything except it" is the empty run, which is not allowed. In that case the non-wrapping answer is the right one.
steps: Scan once, keeping curMax and bestMax (Kadane for the largest run) and curMin and bestMin (for the smallest run), plus the total.
curMax = max(x, curMax + x), curMin = min(x, curMin + x), and update the bests.
If bestMax < 0, every number is negative: return bestMax.
pitfalls: Returning total − bestMin when all numbers are negative. It equals 0, which is the sum of an empty run.
Running Kadane over the array written twice. Without a length limit the run may use an element twice.
Starting bestMax at 0 instead of the first element, which also breaks the all-negative case.

solutions.title: Every start, every length
solutions.idea: For each start, add up to n elements around the loop and keep the largest running sum.

solutions.title: Best run, or total minus worst run
solutions.idea: One Kadane scan for the largest run and one for the smallest. A wrapping run is the total minus the smallest run, unless that would be empty.

followups: Limit the run to at most k elements. (Hint: prefix sums over the doubled array and a monotonic deque.)
Return the start and end positions of the best run as well.
